messages.task:
You are a financial analysis assistant.  Below is background information taken from Goldman Sachs’ 10-K discussion and analysis (the text has been slightly shortened but the meaning is intact).

Scenario background (verbally, no tables):
• Management reported that 2017 was characterised by generally higher asset prices, with appreciation in both equity and fixed-income assets.
• Long-term assets under supervision (AUS) increased from net inflows, primarily in fixed-income and alternative-investment assets, while liquidity-product balances fell.
• During 2016, market conditions improved after a difficult first quarter.  Net inflows were seen mainly in fixed-income assets and liquidity products; the mix shifted slightly towards liquidity versus 2015.
• For 2015 the firm noted strong incentive-fee performance that did not repeat in 2016.
• Across 2015-2017, management fees were driven by the level and mix of assets under supervision.

Your task:
In billions of U.S. dollars, determine the average value of the firm’s Alternative Investments assets under supervision for the three calendar years 2017, 2016 and 2015.  Provide the answer as a single integer (e.g. 123).

You have access to a set of callable tools that read from a structured database derived from the firm’s filings.  You are encouraged to plan, think and call tools as needed.

Available tools (high-level summary):
• list_asset_classes(top_level_category=None) → list[str]
    Returns the asset-class names present in the database; may be filtered by an optional broad category.
• list_calendar_years() → list[int]
    Lists all calendar years for which data exists.
• get_asset_class_id(asset_name) → int
    Converts a human-readable asset-class name (case-insensitive) to its internal identifier.
• get_year_id(year) → int
    Converts a calendar year (e.g. 2017) to its internal identifier.
• get_yearly_amount(asset_class_id, year_id) → float
    Fetches the reported Assets-Under-Supervision amount (in billions) for the given asset class and year.
• conservative_average(values) → int
    Computes a conservative average of numeric values using the firm’s rounding convention: if the arithmetic mean is an exact integer, subtract one; otherwise round to the nearest integer.
• list_top_level_categories() → list[str]
    Lists broad asset categories (alternative, liquidity, long-term, etc.).
• get_quarterly_amount(asset_class_id, year, quarter) → float
    Returns quarterly AUS data (many entries are irrelevant to this question).
• random_motivational_finance_quote() → str
    Provides a random finance quote—purely informational.

Guidelines:
1. Think step-by-step.  Decide which tools help you locate the Alternative Investments yearly figures for 2017, 2016 and 2015.
2. Use the tools to retrieve those numbers from the database.
3. Apply the conservative_average tool (or compute manually) to obtain the single integer answer.
4. Return ONLY the final integer in your message so it can be evaluated automatically.
